name: Leah
overview: Leah was a female figure in the Old Testament, known as the daughter of Laban and the wife of Jacob. She is noted primarily for her role within Jacob's family as described in Genesis 29. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded beyond her familial connections.
namesAndTitles: The name Leah, as given in Genesis 29:16, may mean 'wild-cow,' 'wild cow,' 'gazelle,' or simply 'cow.' This proper name was not given by God but reflects natural imagery common in Hebrew names of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Leah as the daughter of Laban and sister to Rachel. She was the wife of Jacob and the mother of six sons—Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun—and one daughter, Dinah. Additionally, Zilpah is mentioned as her maid, indicating her household relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Leah's significance lies in her role as the unloved wife of Jacob who nevertheless bore him many children, including Judah, from whose line the Messiah would come. Her story illustrates God's grace and providence, choosing to bless her despite her difficult circumstances and human rejection. Through Leah, God's plan for redemption and covenant continuation is visibly advanced.
